manifest.name: dsh-auto-maximize
manifest.description: Automatically maximizes the DeepSeek Harness desktop window on startup (equivalent to clicking the maximize button). · DSH 桌面版启动时自动最大化主窗口（等价于手动点一次最大化）。
manifest.author: FideFei

bundle.text:
# dsh-auto-maximize bundle patch — inserts the host plugin into the profile.
# The plugin maximizes the desktop window shortly after the app starts,
# equivalent to the user clicking the maximize button once.
- insert:
    - id: auto-maximize
      name: dsh-auto-maximize
      config:
        enabled: true
        # auto → in-process FFI first, PowerShell fallback; ffi / powershell force one.
        engine: auto
        # The window normally appears within 1s of launch; 5s without one means
        # something is wrong, so waiting longer is pointless.
        timeoutMs: 5000
        # Keep the last few startups in the diagnostic log: 5 covers a restart
        # loop while staying small (one block per startup, ~1 KB each).
        logKeepRuns: 5

readme.text:
DeepSeek Harness 桌面版插件：启动自动最大化主窗口（等同于手动点击最大化按钮）

适用于 DSH desktop profile，以及所有基于 Electron / 系统窗口运行 DSH 的场景。

插件是 host-only 插件，随桌面版 host 进程在应用启动时加载。host 进程是 Node 子进程
（`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`，由 Electron 主进程拉起），拿不到 `BrowserWindow`，
因此按平台调用系统级「最大化」能力，全部**尽力而为、失败只记日志、绝不 crash host**：

| 平台 | 策略 | 依赖 | 备注 | |---|---|---|---| | Windows | ① 进程内 FFI：宿主同一进程里用 DSH 自带的 koffi 调 Win32 `ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_MAXIMIZE)`
② 回退：pwsh 7 → Windows PowerShell 5.1 子进程 | ① 无（koffi 随 DSH 安装）
② pwsh 7，缺失时自动用 5.1（Windows 自带） | ① 不再起子进程，实测 60–210ms（本来就已最大化时 ~60ms；真正切换含一次 200ms 校验等待）；koffi 不可用时自动回退 ②。PowerShell 按 PATH 解析、不写死安装路径 | | macOS | 把窗口设为主屏可视区大小（`NSScreen.visibleFrame`，即「向窗口发送最大化指令」）；该调用失败时再点击绿色 `AXZoomButton` 作为补救 | `osascript`（系统自带） | 需要「辅助功能/Accessibility」授权，未授权会给出指引日志；`processName` 可覆盖应用名 | | Linux | `wmctrl` → `xdotool` 设置 `_NET_WM_STATE_MAXIMIZED` | 通常**未预装**，需自行安装 | 尽力而为；两者都缺则跳过 |

窗口定位（Windows）：先用 `QueryFullProcessImageNameW` 取窗口所属进程的**镜像路径**，只认与宿主
同一可执行文件的窗口；同镜像多窗口时优先 pid = 宿主父进程（Electron 主进程），再按面积取最大
（主窗口，不是欢迎小窗）。只考虑带 `WS_MAXIMIZEBOX` 的窗口。FFI 路径拿不到结果时，回退的
PowerShell 策略仍按「父进程 PID + 可执行路径」定位。

**为什么不能直接调 `BrowserWindow.maximize()`**：host 进程是纯 Node（`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`，
实测 `require('electron')` 抛 `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`），插件只能拿到系统级窗口句柄——因此「自动最大化」
被实现为「等价于用户点击一次最大化按钮」的系统调用，而非 Electron API 调用。

**FFI 的依赖来源**：`koffi` 是 DSH 桌面版**自带**的运行时依赖
（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-host` 的 dependencies，原生二进制在 `app.asar.unpacked` 内，
desktop-host 自己的 `cli.js` 就用它装 Ctrl-C handler）。插件只是借用 DSH 安装里的这一份，
包本身仍是零运行时依赖。

readme.section: 方式一：通过插件市场 / npm（推荐，发布后可用）
readme.text:
```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-auto-maximize
```

readme.section: 方式二：本地工程安装（开发调试）

readme.text:
在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 中覆盖 `auto-maximize` 行即可：

```yaml
- id: auto-maximize
  config:
    enabled: false        # 禁用
    engine: auto          # Windows 策略：auto | ffi | powershell（默认 auto）

配置项：

| 配置 | 类型 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false` 时整个插件不做事 |
| `engine` | `'auto'` \| `'ffi'` \| `'powershell'` | `'auto'` | Windows 策略：`auto`＝进程内 FFI 优先、失败回退子进程；`ffi`／`powershell` 强制只用其一（排查用） |
| `timeoutMs` | number | `5000` | 启动后持续寻找窗口的最长时间（毫秒）。窗口正常在启动后 1s 内出现，5s 还没等到基本可判定异常；`engine: auto` 下 FFI 与 PowerShell 各自计时，最坏情况约 2 倍 |
| `processName` | string | 可执行文件名 | macOS/Linux 定位窗口用的进程/窗口标题名 |
| `logFile` | boolean \| string | `~/.dsh/auto-maximize.log` | 诊断日志：`false` 关闭文件日志；字符串指定自定义路径；删除文件即清空 |
| `logKeepRuns` | number | `5` | 日志文件里保留最近几次启动（每次启动一个 `===== … =====` 分隔块） |
| `logKeepLines` | number | `200` | 单个运行块最多保留多少行（超出时丢中间、保留开头与最近的尾部；当前块写满即停） |

macOS 出于安全限制，用 `osascript`（System Events）控制其他 App 的窗口必须先获得
**「辅助功能 / Accessibility」**授权。

> ⚠️ **注意事项：指令形式同样需要授权。** 插件把窗口直接设为 `set position/size`（「向窗口发送
> 最大化指令」）还是点击 `AXZoomButton`，**两种方式都走同一套 macOS Accessibility API，都需要
> 辅助功能授权**。原因：要挪动另一个进程的窗口只能走该 API，系统的闸门拦的是 API 本身、不是进程
> 身份——哪怕 `osascript` 是 DSH 自己的子进程也一样（TCC 会把授权追溯归属到 DSH 应用，所以勾选
> DeepSeek Harness 即可覆盖它，但这并不豁免授权）。**换成 Windows 那样的进程内 FFI 也绕不过**：
> macOS 没有「给窗口发个消息就能最大化」的跨进程调用，zoom 只能经 Accessibility API，而那正是被
> 授权闸门拦住的入口。真正免授权的路径只有让 DSH 主进程自己调 `BrowserWindow.maximize()`
> （启动参数 / host→main IPC），需要 DSH 本体提供通道，插件作为外部方做不到。**因此请保留授权**。

插件未获授权时会在 host 日志输出指引（关键字 `dsh-auto-maximize`），按以下步骤授权后重启即可：

1. 打开 **系统设置 → 隐私与安全性 → 辅助功能**；
2. 勾选 **DeepSeek Harness**（以及承载/启动它的终端或启动器，如有）；
3. 重启 DeepSeek Harness（授权对已运行的进程不生效）。

仍无效时，可用 `processName` 指定实际的进程名——打包后应用显示名可能与可执行文件名不同。

**诊断日志**：插件每一步都会写入 `~/.dsh/auto-maximize.log`
（Windows：`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\auto-maximize.log`）。**只有一个文件，最新的运行在最上面**：
每块以 `===== 时间 run(pid=…, version=…) =====` 开头，下面是本次启动的日志；保留最近
`logKeepRuns` 次启动（默认 5），单个运行块最多 `logKeepLines` 行（默认 200，超出时丢中间、
保留表头与最近的尾部）。顺序按表头时间戳判定，文件被手工调换顺序也能正确归位；表头不可解析
（手改坏了、乱码、旧格式残留）的块按「最旧」处理，会在下次启动时被淘汰，不会影响本次记录。
排查「没生效」时直接看这个文件：Windows 上会看到 `ffi: koffi … via …` /
`ffi: maximized hwnd=…` / `koffi unavailable`，macOS 上会看到 `perm:`（缺授权）/
`nowindow:`（没找到窗口）/ `maximized-bounds`（成功）。不需要日志时用 `logFile: false` 关闭，
或直接删除该文件清空。

> 对比：**Windows 端不需要任何额外权限**——`ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_MAXIMIZE)` 是直接 Win32 API
> 调用（非模拟点击），对同一用户的窗口无需提权。
>
> **macOS 为什么没有对应的「进程内」路径**：Windows 的最大化是发给窗口的消息，任何进程都能对
> 任意 `hwnd` 调用；macOS 的 zoom 是窗口对象（AppKit `NSWindow`）自己的操作，跨进程只能走
> Accessibility API（`AXUIElement` + `kAXZoomAction`），而调用 Accessibility API **本身就需要
> 辅助功能授权**。所以 macOS 上只有「系统 API + 授权」这一条路——进程内 FFI 既省不掉授权，也
> 换不来新能力，这正是本插件在 macOS 上仍走 osascript 的原因。

从 profile 的 `package.json` 两处（`dependencies` + `dsh.profile.bundles`）移除
`dsh-auto-maximize`，再执行 `pnpm install`，重启应用。

```sh
npm install   # 包本身无第三方运行时依赖（FFI 借用 DSH 自带的 koffi）；dev 仅测试需要 node:test
npm test      # 36 条：模块加载 / 禁用分支 / 效果注册 / koffi 锚点回退 / 窗口挑选 / 引擎顺序 /
              # 日志开关 / 免重启验证脚本
npm pack      # 生成可发布的 tarball（prepack 会先跑测试）

测试与打包都用 `DSH_AUTO_MAXIMIZE_NO_LOG=1` 关掉文件日志，不会写、也不会轮转你真实的
`~/.dsh/auto-maximize.log`。

插件是「每次挂载跑一次」：cordis 调用 `apply()` 时把当时已存在的窗口最大化一次。所以**重新挂载
bundle 就等于重跑插件**——「设置 → 插件」里关掉再打开即可，不必重启桌面版。
`scripts/verify-live.ps1` 就按这个方式检查：读日志里最新一次挂载，再用 Win32 独立确认窗口真的
最大化了。

```sh
npm login                                   # 首次
npm publish --registry https://registry.npmjs.org
```

发布后即可在 [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) 插件市场的
「申请收录插件 ↗」入口提交收录（指向 [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin)
的 `data/plugins/<owner>__<repo>.yml`，见 [提交指南](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/blob/main/contributing.md)）。

- 仅在桌面版（desktop profile）有意义；web profile 无窗口，插件会安静跳过。
- 只启动时执行一次，不会干预会话中手动调整的窗口状态。
- macOS 必须先给 DeepSeek Harness 授予「辅助功能」权限，否则只会写出授权指引日志；Linux 需要
  自备 `wmctrl` 或 `xdotool`。
- 多实例/多窗口：Windows 上先用「镜像路径」精确认领本实例的窗口，再按「pid = 宿主父进程」收敛，
  多个 DSH 实例互不干扰；只有当本镜像没有任何窗口时才换下一个引擎。macOS/Linux 取
  「最前端/首个匹配」窗口，多开时建议用 `processName` 区分。
- 失败只写 host 日志（关键字 `dsh-auto-maximize`），不影响应用运行。

- **设置 UI 开关**：把 `enabled` 接进「设置 → 通用设置」。当前为 host-only 插件，只能通过
  `cordis.patch.yml` 配置；做成界面开关需要 client-plugin 侧的设置面板扩展。
- **启动参数 / host↔main IPC**：让 DSH 本体提供 `--maximize` 之类的开关，或在 host→main 的 IPC
  白名单里放行窗口控制消息（当前白名单只有 `update-tasks` / `quit-inspection` / `ready` /
  `shutdown-complete` / `platform-session`，发别的会被 SIGTERM）。这属于上游改动，插件侧做不到。
  详见下方「已排查：为什么没有走 DSH 自身通道」。
- **正式图标**：`assets/icon.svg` 为占位设计（最大化双框图形），欢迎替换为正式图标。

readme.section: 已排查：为什么没有走 DSH 自身通道
readme.text:
- Electron 主进程没有窗口开关：全文件只识别 `process.argv.includes("--updated")`，窗口尺寸写死
  `1280×820`，没有窗口状态持久化，桌面设置文件只接受 `updates.allowTestAuthPopupWindow`。
- 二次启动带参数无效：`requestSingleInstanceLock()` 的 `second-instance` 只做聚焦，参数不会传给已有窗口。
- `dsh` CLI 的旗标到不了窗口：桌面 profile 被明确禁止从 CLI 启动
  （`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`）。

---

**仓库**：Gitee（主）<https://gitee.com/FideFei/dsh-auto-maximize> ｜ GitHub（镜像）<https://github.com/FideFeiPlane/dsh-auto-maximize>
[MIT](LICENSE) © FideFei

DeepSeek Harness desktop plugin: **automatically maximizes the main window on startup** (equivalent to clicking the maximize button once).

Works with the DSH desktop app (desktop profile) and any scenario where DSH runs inside an Electron/system window.

The plugin is host-only: it loads in the host process at app startup. The host is a Node child process
(`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, spawned by the Electron main process that owns the window), so it can never
call `BrowserWindow.maximize()` — instead it uses per-platform OS-level maximize. Everything is
**best-effort: on failure it logs a warning and never crashes the host**:

| Platform | Strategy | Dependency | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | Windows | ① In-process FFI: call Win32 `ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_MAXIMIZE)` from the host's own process via the koffi that ships with DSH
② Fallback: **pwsh 7** → **Windows PowerShell 5.1** child process | ① none (koffi ships with DSH)
② pwsh 7, falls back to 5.1 (always present on Windows) | ① no subprocess, measured 60–210 ms (about 60 ms when the window is already maximized; a real transition includes one 200 ms verification wait); falls back to ② when koffi is unavailable. PowerShell is resolved via PATH, no hardcoded install path | | macOS | Resize the window to the main screen's visible frame (`NSScreen.visibleFrame` — i.e. "send the window a maximize instruction"); if that fails, click the green `AXZoomButton` as a remedy | `osascript` (built-in) | Requires Accessibility permission for the caller; a grant guide is logged when missing. Override the app name with `processName`. | | Linux | `wmctrl` → `xdotool` set `_NET_WM_STATE_MAXIMIZED` | usually **not preinstalled** | Best-effort; skips silently if both are missing. |

Window lookup (Windows): resolve each window's owning process **image path** with
`QueryFullProcessImageNameW` and accept only windows owned by the same executable as the host; among
several, prefer `pid == host parent` (the Electron main process), then the largest area (the main
window, not the welcome window). Only windows with `WS_MAXIMIZEBOX` qualify. If FFI finds nothing, the
PowerShell fallback still locates by "host parent PID + executable path".

**Why not `BrowserWindow.maximize()`:** the host process is plain Node (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`,
`require('electron')` throws `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`), so plugins can only reach OS-level window handles.
"Auto maximize" is implemented as "equivalent to the user clicking the maximize button once" via
system calls, not an Electron API call.

**Where the FFI dependency comes from:** `koffi` is a runtime dependency **already shipped with the
DSH desktop app** (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-host`'s dependencies; the native binary lives in
`app.asar.unpacked`, and desktop-host's own `cli.js` uses it to install the Ctrl-C handler). The
plugin only borrows the copy inside the DSH installation, so the package stays free of third-party
runtime dependencies.

readme.section: Option 1: from the plugin market / npm (once published)
readme.text:
```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-auto-maximize
```

Override the `auto-maximize` row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: auto-maximize
  config:
    enabled: false        # disable
    engine: auto          # Windows strategy: auto | ffi | powershell (default auto)

Options:

| Config | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `true` | `false` disables the plugin entirely |
| `engine` | `'auto'` \| `'ffi'` \| `'powershell'` | `'auto'` | Windows strategy: `auto` = in-process FFI first, PowerShell on failure; `ffi` / `powershell` force one (for diagnosis) |
| `timeoutMs` | number | `5000` | max time to keep looking for the window (ms). It normally appears within 1s of launch, so 5s without one means something is wrong; under `engine: auto` FFI and PowerShell time out independently, so the worst case is about 2× |
| `processName` | string | executable basename | process/window name to match on macOS/Linux |
| `logFile` | boolean \| string | `~/.dsh/auto-maximize.log` | diagnostic log: `false` disables file logging; a string relocates it; delete the file to clear it |
| `logKeepRuns` | number | `5` | how many recent runs to keep in the log file (one `===== … =====` block per startup) |
| `logKeepLines` | number | `200` | max lines per run block (overflow drops the middle, keeping the header and the most recent tail; the current block stops once full) |

On macOS, controlling another app's windows via `osascript` (System Events) requires
**Accessibility** permission. When it is missing the plugin logs a guide (keyword
`dsh-auto-maximize`). Grant it like this, then restart:

1. Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility**.
2. Enable **DeepSeek Harness** (and the terminal/launcher that hosts it, if any).
3. Restart DeepSeek Harness (the grant does not affect already-running processes).

> ⚠️ **Note: the "instruction form" also needs the permission.** Whether the plugin resizes
> the window directly (`set position/size` — "send the window a maximize instruction") or
> clicks `AXZoomButton`, **both go through the same macOS Accessibility API and both need the
> Accessibility grant**. Why: the only way to move another process's window is that API — the
> system's gate is on the API itself, not on process identity. Even though `osascript` is DSH's
> own child process, TCC attributes the grant to the DSH app (so enabling DeepSeek Harness covers
> it), but it does not waive the grant. **The Windows-style in-process FFI does not bypass it
> either**: macOS has no cross-process "post a message and the window maximizes" call, so zoom
> can only go through the Accessibility API — exactly the entry the grant gates. The only
> permission-free route is DSH maximizing its own window inside its own process (a startup flag /
> host→main IPC calling `BrowserWindow.maximize()`) — that needs a DSH-provided channel, which an
> external plugin cannot offer. **Keep the grant.**

If it still does not work, set `processName` to the real process name — a packaged app's
display name can differ from its executable's basename.

**Diagnostic log**: every step is written to `~/.dsh/auto-maximize.log`
(Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\auto-maximize.log`). **One file only, newest run on top**: each block
starts with `===== <time> run(pid=…, version=…) =====` followed by that startup's lines; the last
`logKeepRuns` runs are kept (default 5), and each block is capped at `logKeepLines` lines (default
200 — the middle is dropped, the header and the most recent tail are kept). Blocks are ordered by the
timestamp in their header, so a hand-edited file is re-ordered correctly; a block whose header cannot
be parsed (corrupted, garbage, legacy remnant) counts as oldest and is evicted on the next startup.
When maximize "doesn't work", open this file: on Windows you will see `ffi: koffi … via …` /
`ffi: maximized hwnd=…` / `koffi unavailable`, on macOS the `osascript` result — `perm:` (missing
permission) / `nowindow:` (window not found) / `maximized-bounds` (success). Disable it with
`logFile: false`, or delete the file to clear it.

> By contrast, **Windows needs no extra permission**: `ShowWindow(hwnd, SW_MAXIMIZE)` is a
> direct Win32 API call (not simulated clicks) and needs no elevation for the user's own window.
>
> **Why macOS has no equivalent in-process path**: on Windows, maximizing is a message sent to a
> window, so any process may call it for any `hwnd`. On macOS, zoom is an operation of the window
> object itself (`NSWindow`), and cross-process access is only possible through the Accessibility
> API (`AXUIElement` + `kAXZoomAction`) — which **itself requires Accessibility permission**. So on
> macOS the only route is "system API + permission": in-process FFI would neither remove the
> permission nor add capability, which is why this plugin still uses `osascript` there.

Remove `dsh-auto-maximize` from both places in the profile's `package.json`
(`dependencies` + `dsh.profile.bundles`), run `pnpm install`, restart the app.

```sh
npm install   # the package has no third-party runtime deps (FFI borrows DSH's own koffi); dev only needs node:test
npm test      # 36 cases: module load / disabled branch / effect registration / koffi anchor
              # fallback / window selection / engine order / log guard / verify-live script
npm pack      # build the publishable tarball (prepack runs the tests first)

Tests and packaging run with `DSH_AUTO_MAXIMIZE_NO_LOG=1`, so they never write to or rotate your real
`~/.dsh/auto-maximize.log`.

The plugin runs **once per mount**: cordis calls `apply()`, which maximizes whatever window exists at
that moment. Re-mounting the bundle therefore re-runs it — toggle it off and on in Settings → Plugins,
no app restart needed. `scripts/verify-live.ps1` checks exactly that way: it reads the newest mount
from the log and then confirms with Win32 that the window is really maximized.

```sh
npm login                                   # first time
npm publish --registry https://registry.npmjs.org
```

Once published, submit the plugin for listing in [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market)
via its "Submit a plugin ↗" link (a `data/plugins/<owner>__<repo>.yml` file in
[awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) — see
[contributing.md](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/blob/main/contributing.md)).

- Only meaningful in the desktop profile; a web profile has no window and the plugin skips silently.
- Runs once at startup; never touches window state you change during a session.
- macOS requires granting Accessibility permission to DeepSeek Harness first, otherwise only a
  permission guide is logged; Linux needs `wmctrl` or `xdotool` installed.
- Multi-instance/multi-window: on Windows it first claims this instance's window by **image path**,
  then prefers `pid == host parent`, so multiple DSH instances don't interfere; only when this image
  owns no window does it move to the next engine. macOS/Linux take the "frontmost / first match"
  window — use `processName` to disambiguate when running several instances.
- On failure only writes to the host log (keyword `dsh-auto-maximize`); the app keeps running.

- **Settings UI toggle**: wire `enabled` into "Settings → General". The plugin is host-only and
  currently reads `cordis.patch.yml` only; a UI switch needs a client-plugin settings panel.
- **Startup flag / host↔main IPC**: have DSH itself expose `--maximize`, or allow window-control
  messages through the host→main IPC whitelist (currently only `update-tasks` / `quit-inspection` /
  `ready` / `shutdown-complete` / `platform-session`; anything else gets SIGTERM). That is an
  upstream change a plugin cannot make. See "Investigated: why not DSH's own channel" below.
- **Official icon**: `assets/icon.svg` is a placeholder maximize glyph — a real icon is welcome.

readme.section: Investigated: why not DSH's own channel
readme.text:
- The Electron main process has no window switch: it reads only `process.argv.includes("--updated")`,
  hardcodes a `1280×820` window, persists no window state, and its desktop settings file accepts only
  `updates.allowTestAuthPopupWindow`.
- Relaunching with flags does nothing: `requestSingleInstanceLock()`'s `second-instance` handler only
  focuses the window; the new arguments never reach the existing one.
- `dsh` CLI flags cannot reach the window: booting the desktop profile from the CLI is refused
  (`profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`).
